clue.text: Contract in a card game

parts.note: bridge is the classic partnership card game of bidding and tricks

explanation.surface: A player describes a bid made during a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a bridge term, which fits the surface perfectly, but here it is the verb meaning to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text by cutting it down is to contract it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: African city is large and confusing

indicators.note: confusing suggests the letters of the words before it are jumbled up into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a North African city big and bewildering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges the seven letters of IS LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Algeria is a large port city on the North African coast.

clue.text: Making haste, goes for minor adjustments

parts.note: someone making haste is hurrying along, running
to repair to a place is an old-fashioned way of saying one goes there

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying off to sort out small tweaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairs to' in the sense of 'betakes oneself to' is a formal, slightly old idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fixes made while a machine stays in use are the classic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: At a disadvantage with this type of clue

explanation.definitionFit: Being behind in a contest is being low; and this clue sits in the vertical half of the grid.

clue.text: Recorded tree fell in the end

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled tree sits within the other piece

parts.note: end taken as the word itself

indicators.note: fell here is the adjective meaning cruel or savage, so the word tree is treated roughly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree finally came down, as the record shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but here it is the old adjective meaning savage, the anagram signal; 'in' places the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing something into a ledger or log is putting it on record.

clue.text: Poor gypsies hold wild party

indicators.note: hold signals that the words before it contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Impoverished travellers throw a raucous party.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of poOR GYpsies.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild party is a debauched revel, an occasion of unrestrained indulgence.

clue.text: One with head in sand? That's no way to get wealthy

parts.note: O is a zero, nought, so no
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: Burying your head in the sand will never make you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the folk belief that this big flightless bird hides its head in sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless bird is popularly, though wrongly, said to bury its head when frightened.

clue.text: Finally joining general rejoicing

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word joining

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Everyone ends up taking part in the celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight, a near synonym of joyful celebration.

clue.text: Left with sweet-sounding fawn, perhaps

parts.note: red is a political label for the left wing

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for sweet is heard, not written, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sweet person is a dear

explanation.surface: Someone is left with a charming young fawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A fawn is a young deer, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example of the species.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawn is a young deer, and this large British species has fawns, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Alter campanologist's target?

explanation.definitionFit: To vary things is the idiom's sense; a campanologist, a bell-ringer, aims to sound sequences of bells.

clue.text: Breezed off to see romantic film?

explanation.definitionFit: Departed on the breeze, carried away by air; and the 1939 epic romance starring Vivien Leigh.

clue.text: Issue period return

indicators.note: return asks for the word for period to be read backwards

parts.note: a period is a span of time

explanation.surface: A complaint about a period of service being sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a sound or gas is to give it out, send it forth.

clue.text: Fall behind, right in the rear

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for right inside the word for rear

parts.note: the tail is the back end, the rear

explanation.surface: A runner drops back and ends up at the very back.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag in a race is to be behind the leader.

clue.text: Type of illness universal in later years

indicators.note: in puts the letter for universal inside the word for old years

parts.note: one's later years are old age
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A common complaint of growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, universal.
explanation.definitionFit: A malarial fever with shivering fits is an old-fashioned sickness.

clue.text: Union's reparation?

parts.note: making amends is literally becoming united again, as if the word for amends were built from being joined as one

explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to restore unity with whoever was wronged.

clue.text: Regularly visit Henry, a relative

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone often drops in on Henry and an aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to go there often, as ghosts are said to.

clue.text: Able to see the digs need repair

indicators.note: need repair suggests the letters are broken and must be put back together differently

explanation.surface: An observer notes that the lodgings need fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' is British slang for lodgings; 'need repair' rearranges THE DIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with working eyesight, not blind, is the sense.

clue.text: Warmth applied to woman's plant

parts.note: warmth means heat
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A gardener warms a woman's shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Heath-land ling is a low shrub with purple flowers.

clue.text: Check detains one, before man returns from Asian country

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next one
detains means the check word holds the numeral for one inside it

parts.note: to vet is to check
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: returns asks for the word man to be read backwards

parts.note: man taken as written

explanation.surface: A border check holds one traveller before a man is sent back from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Southeast Asian nation with its capital at Hanoi.

clue.text: Sister in cheap dress is in sight

indicators.note: in puts the word for sister inside the word for cheap

parts.note: something cheap and nasty is vile
a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister

explanation.surface: A sister wearing a cheap frock stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be seen is in view.

clue.text: Authority for chap to take appointment

parts.note: a chap is a man
an appointment is a date

explanation.surface: Permission for a man to keep a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is the power given by voters or superiors to act, an authorisation.

clue.text: Criticise a revolutionary's grand style

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a revolutionary's showy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence, a dashing flair.

clue.text: Clown is dreadful, I report

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the words that follow are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A reviewer writes that a circus clown was awful.
explanation.definitionFit: The sad white-faced figure of French pantomime is a classic clown character.

clue.text: Mountain where our mother has to relax

parts.note: Eve is the biblical first woman, mother of us all
to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: A family names the peak where Mum has to take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest peak, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Blow second circuit

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A boxer takes a hit on the second time round the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack with an open hand is a kind of strike.

clue.text: Starting a violent attack

explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something; and an assault or onslaught, an older military sense.

clue.text: Glen, goodbye!

explanation.definitionFit: A valley, as in poetry; and the Latin word of farewell.

clue.text: Ponder one way to prepare wine

explanation.definitionFit: To think something over; and to heat wine with spices and sugar.

clue.text: Brought up a little bit of information

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a small item of news.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for study are the plural of datum.

clue.text: The main area of alleged disappearances

definitions.text: The main area of alleged disappearances

parts.words: The main area of alleged disappearances
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is a stretch of ocean where ships and planes are said to have vanished

explanation.definitionFit: A region of the western Atlantic, between Miami, Puerto Rico and an island colony, notorious for vanishings.

clue.text: Conservative is depressed

explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tory party colour signals right-wing politics; and feeling low or sad.

clue.text: Going over Tristan in translation

indicators.note: in translation suggests the name is turned into another form, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Discussing Wagner's opera, rendered into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: Tristan is the hero of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage across or through a place, the act of crossing.
